newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl to raise human rights on Indonesian visit.
newsitem.headline: Kohl to raise human rights on Indonesian visit.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl plans to raise the issue of human rights with Indonesian government leaders during his official visit to Jakarta later this month, a German government spokesman said on Monday.
Kohl, who has met Indonesian President Suharto several times in the past, will visit Jakarta from October 25 to 29.

Spokesman Peter Hausmann's comments came after this year's Nobel Peace Prize winner Jose Ramos-Horta, an East Timor independence activist, told Deutsche Welle radio he hoped Germany would use its influence in Indonesia to help reduce tension in East Timor.

"No other country in Europe has the weight, the influence on Indonesia as Germany," Ramos-Horta told Deutsche Welle on Monday. He said he would "find it strange" if Kohl did not put more pressure on Indonesia over East Timor, human rights and democracy.

Ramos-Horta and East Timor's Catholic Bishop Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo won the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize jointly for their efforts to bring peace in the territory which Indonesia invaded after Portuguese colonisers left in 1975.
